name: local-missed-requirement
about: A local job whose earlier leads often missed a hard requirement or gave a wrong number.

area.label: Fixture Yard, IL
area.reason: Fixture: drivers within a day's drive of the yard.

history.text: Boostpoint 2026 benchmark, CDL drivers on Meta: an ad costing more than $42.00 per lead after 5 leads, or $85.00 spent with no lead, is where pausing is suggested.
Of 58 of our ad leads in the last 28 days, 44 were called and 25 were reached.
21 of 58 of our ad leads in the last 28 days did not meet a hard requirement of the opening.
9 of the 44 ad leads we called in the last 28 days had a wrong number.

output.audience: Class A drivers with the years of experience the opening states, who want local delivery work on hourly pay and a weekday schedule that ends at home. They will stop for an ad that states the pay, the schedule and the touch freight plainly, so they can tell at a glance whether they qualify.

angles.idea: Lead with the hourly pay rate for local Class A delivery, shown over a day cab out on a local road.
angles.proof: The opening states its pay per hour and that the work is local delivery in a day cab.
angles.why: Hourly pay is the clearest fact of this job for a local driver. No hook or scene has been measured for this carrier yet, so this is a starting point, not a proven winner.

angles.idea: Lead with being home daily on a Monday to Friday week, pictured as the home street a driver returns to when the shift ends.
angles.proof: The opening offers home daily and a Monday to Friday schedule.
angles.why: The home-time and the working week are what set this job apart for a driver weighing local work. Nothing has been measured for this hook yet.

angles.idea: Lead with the day cab parked at the end of a shift, the plain sign that this is local delivery work.
angles.proof: The opening is a local delivery job run in a day cab, and it offers health insurance.
angles.why: A day cab shows the kind of work before any words do, and the health insurance can sit under it as a supporting line. Untested here, so treat it as a trial.

angles.idea: Say plainly who this job is for: a Class A licence, the years of experience the opening states, and touch freight on the route.
angles.proof: The opening states a Class A licence, a years requirement and touch freight.
angles.why: A large share of recent leads did not meet a hard requirement, so stating the requirements and the touch freight up front should cut wasted calls. It filters more than it attracts.
